book_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
question: Does the November 20, 2026 multi-timeframe tape show a Stage 2 base or a Stage 4 breakdown that forbids new risk?

epigraph.quote: The tape is evidence, not an argument.
epigraph.author: Research Desk maxim

web_blocks.html: Bloom Energy's chart moved from a damaged transition on November 12 into a clear Stage 4 breakdown on November 20, 2026. The market-facts ledger closes BE at $142.39 [57]. That is down 15.30% on the day, 25.83% on the week, 34.61% on the month, and 59.47% below its $351.28 high [57]. TradingView records $142.45 (-15.26% daily, -28.93% weekly), a six-cent tape difference [55]. Heavy selling pushed volume to 28.55 million shares (1.57x average; 1.80x on Finviz) with ten distribution days in 25 sessions [56][57].

Our two feeds label the Weinstein stage differently, so we disclose both cleanly. The market-facts ledger tags BE as Stage 1 (Basing) only because the 50-day SMA ($234.02) stays above the 200-day SMA ($223.89) [57]. Yet that 50-day average fell from $249.16 twenty-one sessions ago and $246.07 ten sessions ago [57]. Price now sits 39.13% below the falling 50-day SMA, 36.38% below the 200-day SMA, and 41.30% below the 30-week SMA ($242.68) [55]. The Stage 2 evaluator therefore assigns STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, CAP_REJECTED), which governs our risk control [55].

web_blocks.takeaway: Every timeframe from 4-hour to weekly confirms active distribution below falling structural averages. Even though daily RSI (32.43) and 4-hour RSI (27.94) look stretched, the 4-hour chart shows zero upward turn and heavy volume confirms forced liquidation.

web_blocks.html: Market regime and options flow reinforce caution. On November 20, SPY closed at $689.81 (-3.64% daily, -11.75% off its high) below its 50-day ($760.18) and 200-day ($732.76) averages with nine distribution days [57]. Koyfin confirmed the S&P 500 in correction, down 11.6% from its October 6 peak [53]. QQQ fell 20.24% off its peak and IWM entered Stage 4 [57]. Cboe showed heavy hedging with a 1.13 total put/call ratio and 1.41 SPX ratio [54]. Our options scanner outputs NO_OPTIONS_EDGE for BE due to broken moving averages and conditional fundamentals [55].

Breaching the prior structural floor ends the tactical trade. Our November 12 dossier set a $158.76 to $163.60 monitor band and a $150.34 stop. Closing at $142.39 ($142.45 TradingView) broke both levels on heavy volume [55][57]. The automated snapshot band ($201.73 to $237.53) now sits overhead as resistance rather than support. Because macOS Chrome automation is unavailable on Linux, our options overlay uses public chain and TradingView feeds instead of live Robinhood tabs.

The chart rules out new entries and mandates an immediate exit on held shares. An oversold 4-hour RSI of 27.94 can spark a sharp bounce toward $161.18 or the $176.73 four-hour EMA, not a sustainable trend. Any future entry requires a multi-week Stage 1 base above $119.19 or $140.69, followed by a high-volume reclaim of the 50-day and 200-day SMAs. Chapter 9 pairs this Stage 4 breakdown with our valuation findings to set the action plan.

book_paragraphs: The chart gives us a clear verdict without guesswork. Between November 12 and November 20, 2026, Bloom Energy broke below its prior support structure. On the market-facts ledger, the stock closed at $142.39 on November 20, down 15.30 percent in one day and 25.83 percent for the week. TradingView recorded $142.45, a tiny six-cent feed difference. Volume jumped to 28.55 million shares, or 1.57 times normal, logging ten distribution days in 25 sessions. That is institutional selling, not quiet basing.

We disclose a stage classification split across our data feeds. The market-facts ledger still tags Bloom as Stage 1 Basing because the 50-day SMA ($234.02) has not crossed below the 200-day SMA ($223.89). That cross lags after a big prior rally. Look at the slope and price gap instead: the 50-day average fell from $249.16 a month ago, and Bloom sits 39 percent below it and 41 percent below its 30-week average ($242.68). Our Stage 2 evaluator therefore assigns STAGE_4 and caps new capital.

All three timeframes confirm the damage. Weekly RSI-14 is 38.43, with price 30 percent below the 10-week EMA ($204.80). Daily RSI-14 is 32.43 with a wide $21.13 daily true range, near 15 percent of price. Four-hour RSI is 27.94 below the 4-hour EMA ($176.73), with no turn upward yet. Oversold readings can cause sharp dead-cat bounces, not safe entries.

The broader tape removes any reason to fight this downtrend. SPY fell 3.64 percent to $689.81, leaving the S&P 500 down 11.6 percent from its October 6 peak. QQQ stood 20 percent off its high, and IWM entered Stage 4. Cboe ratios showed defensive hedging at 1.13 total and 1.41 on the S&P 500. Our options engine sets NO_OPTIONS_EDGE because broken averages and conditional fundamentals forbid call trades.

For existing holders, $150.34 is the decisive line. That was our structural stop in the November 12 dossier. Closing at $142.39 breached that stop cleanly on heavy volume. In a tactical position, a broken stop requires immediate action rather than hoping for a bounce back to cost. Chapter 9 sets out the exact exit and cash plan.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Oversold oscillators tempt buyers into catching falling knives. When price sits 39 percent below a falling 50-day average in a market correction, patience protects capital far better than a hero trade.
